newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

ISRAEL, Nov 12 - Haifa - eight vessels due, 1-2 days delay expected, vessels loading/discharging at berth - 2 general cargo, 2 bulk, 3 containers, 2 tankers, waiting at anchorage to load - 1 general cargo, 3 container vessels, 4 vessels under repairs/drydock, 3 awaiting orders. Ashdod - one to two days delay expected, loading/discharging at berth - 4 general cargo, 2 bulk, 3 containers, 2 passenger vessels, 2 container vessels iting at anchorage to load/discharge. Eilat - vessels loading/discharging at berth - 1 car carrier, 1 passenger vessel.
JORDAN, Nov 9 - Aqaba - no vessels due, no delays expected, 1 vessel loading at berth, 8 vessels discharging at berth, 3 vessels waiting at anchorage to load, 2 vessels awaiting orders.

MAURITIUS, Nov 12 - Port Louis - port working normally. Five vessels alongside of which 2 container vessels discharging and loading, 3 general cargo vessels, 8 fishing vessels to discharge, no idle vessels, 16 vessels due by 19/11.

MOZAMBIQUE, Nov 11 - Nacala - port working normally (first come, first served basis). No restriction on berthing and sailing at night subject to a gratuity to be paid to the pilot. Draft restriction of 9.5 metres plus height of tide at general cargo berths and 14 metres at container berths. One tug available. Beira - general cargo berths working normally (first come, first served). Container Terminal/other terminals working normally. Pilotage now possible 24 hours a day for vessels up to 140 metres LOA with a maximum draft of 7.5 metres. Two tugboats fully operational. Night navigation for larger vessels is restricted and subject to prior arrangements.
NAMIBIA, Nov 11 - Walvis Bay - working normally.
SIERRA LEONE, Nov 11 - Freetown - vessels due - 3 container dischargers, 1 aid cargo discharger, 1 bitumen discharger, 1 relief cargo loader, 1 bulk carrier anchored, no delays expected.

TUNISIA, Nov 9 - Sousse - two vessels in port of which 1 discharging sugar, 1 discharging woodpulp, no waiting time. Sfax - two vessels operating of which 1 discharging bagged sugar, 1 loading bulk TSP. Tunis - one vessel awaiting instructions. Rades - five ro/ros in port. Goulette - north side - 1 vessel (sweeping/dragging). South Side - 1 vessel discharging grain, 1 motor tanker, 1 vessel in roads.
Nov 11 - Bizerta - three vessels operating of which 1 discharging timber, 1 discharging steel, 1 loading cement, no delays, no congestion. Zarzis - no vessels in port, no delays, no congestion.

TURKEY, Nov 11 - Istanbul - Haydarpasa - 9 vessels operating of which 4 containers, 4 dry cargo, 1 ro/ro. Galata - 9 cargo/passenger vessels operating, port congested. Ambarli - 12 vessels operating, port congested.

Nov 12 - Mersin - 17 vessels operating of which loading - 1 citrus, 1 cargo, 1 cotton, 1 potatoes, 1 legumes, 2 cement, 1 livestock, discharging - 1 vehicle, 1 pyrites, 1 container/cargo, 1 paper, 1 sunflower oil, loading/discharging - 1 container/vehicle, 2 containers, 1 container/wool, 11 vessels awaiting orders. No vessels in free zone piers. Seka - one vessel discharging fertiliser. Mersin - 12 vessels operating of which loading - 1 citrus, 1 potatoes, 2 others loading, discharging - 1 paper, 1 cotton, 1 manure, both import and export of 1 vehicle and 4 containers, 14 vessels anchored.

SOUTH AFRICA, Nov 11 - Richards Bay - general cargo berths congested, berthing delays approx 12 hours. Bulk import berths working normally. Bulk export berths (minerals, etc.) working normally. Bulk coal berths - 1 of the coal terminal ship loaders has been taken out of operation until 17/11 for maintenance, considerable congestion expected for vessels awaiting berth turn from 12/11, 72 hours berthing delay can be expected.

Durban - Container Terminal - delays of up to 24 hours at present. Point/New Pier/Maydon wharf berths - general cargo working normally. Maize terminal - 2 sunflower loaders for Nov. Citrus terminal closed 1/11. Bunker supplies - delays of up to 4 hours in supplying of bunkers due to bunching of vessels. Drydock and floating dock booked for Nov. East London - general cargo/combi terminal berths - busy, but no delays expected. Drydock fully booked for Nov and up to 16/12. Copper - moving in small parcels in containers to far east. Elevator - 1 vessel due mid-Nov as oil pipeline under-utilised. Tankers expect to be busy until end-December.

Port Elizabeth - two vessels in port. No delays expected on general, tanker, ore or container berths. One ore vessel due 15/11. Cape Town - breakbulk berths - possible delays of 12-24 hours, due to 5 bulk vessels operating on 16/11. No delays expected at container terminal. Bunker berths - the Duncan dock will be out of commission for ifo supplies from 4/11 to 15/11. Drydock and repair quay fully occupied, booking essential. Saldanha Bay - working normally.

YEMEN, Nov 11 - Hodeidah - all berths occupied, 7 vessels alongside of which 1 bulk wheat, 1 sugar, 1 timber, 1 general cargo/containers, 1 container vessel, 1 general cargo, 1 passenger vessel, 4 vessels anchored of which 2 containers, 1 general cargo, 1 vessel for loading, berthing waiting time - general cargo up to 2 days, bagged cargo up to 4 days, bulk cargo up to 6 days, containers up to 1 day. Mokha - one vessel alongside discharging wheat flour, no vessels anchored, no berthing waiting time.
